hook: In November 2026, the World Meteorological Organization documented extreme global temperatures and melting ice.

sections.voiceover: In November 2026, the World Meteorological Organization documented extreme global temperatures and melting ice.
sections.visual_cue: Global temperature anomaly map showing heat intensity

sections.voiceover: The World Meteorological Organization released this data in Antalya, Türkiye. How much heat is the ocean holding?
sections.visual_cue: WMO report cover in Antalya, Türkiye
b_roll: WMO logo and Antalya conference venue

sections.voiceover: The upper 2000 meters of the ocean absorbed 19 zettajoules of heat, a massive energy increase.
The 2025 ocean heat content exceeded the 2024 value by 19 zettajoules of energy. Antalya, Türkiye, now faces rising sea levels and melting ice as an intense El Niño develops.
sections.visual_cue: Satellite imagery of melting polar ice
b_roll: Satellite footage of melting ice caps

sections.voiceover: The World Meteorological Organization reports a 1.47 degrees Celsius anomaly for January to September 2026.
sections.visual_cue: Close up of a temperature gauge needle in red
